# Nuxt Content

Docs built with Nuxt and the Nuxt Content module, including Docus and Nuxt UI Pro docs templates.

## Detect

- Rendered HTML contains `<div id="__nuxt">` and sets `window.__NUXT__`.
- Static assets load from `/_nuxt/`.
- `<page-url>/_payload.json` returns JSON instead of 404.
- In a repo: `nuxt.config.ts` with `@nuxt/content` (or `@nuxt-themes/docus`) in `modules`, and pages under `content/`.

## Get the source

### From the repo

Pages are markdown in `content/`, written in MDC syntax. Nav order comes from numeric filename prefixes (`1.getting-started/2.installation.md`) and `.navigation.yml` / `_dir.yml` files. Config lives in `nuxt.config.ts` and `app.config.ts`.

### From an export

None; the site is built from the repo.

### From the live site

Each page's `_payload.json` holds the page body as a structured AST ("minimark": `{ type, tag, props, children }` nodes, or compact arrays `[tag, props, ...children]`) plus, usually, the site navigation tree. Convert from this AST, not from rendered HTML.

Mirror `<page-url>/_payload.json` for every page (`mint migrate --topic discovery`, Mirror the raw source). Spot-check one:

```bash
curl -sS https://docs.example.com/guide/setup/_payload.json | python3 -m json.tool | head -60
```

It should show element nodes (`"tag": "h1"` and so on), not HTML. If `_payload.json` 404s site-wide but the site is still Nuxt, look for `_payload.js` and extract the embedded payload with a small Node script before falling back to HTML. Some Nuxt Content sites also expose raw markdown or a query API under `/api/_content/` or `/__nuxt_content/`; prefer raw markdown if it is served.

Pick one URL form during inventory. `/foo` and `/foo/` may both return 200, but usually only one serves `_payload.json`. Mixing them creates duplicate mirror files.

## Config → docs.json

| Nuxt                                           | docs.json                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app.config.ts` site name / `seo.siteName`     | `name`                                                                       |
| `app.config.ts` header logo (light/dark)       | `logo.light`, `logo.dark`                                                    |
| `public/favicon.*`                             | `favicon`                                                                    |
| `app.config.ts` `ui.primary` / theme colors    | `colors.primary` (resolve the named color to its hex from the rendered CSS)  |
| Header links (`header.links`)                  | `navbar.links`, or `navigation.tabs` with `href` if they sit in the main row |
| Footer links / socials                         | `footer.links`, `footer.socials`                                             |
| Top-level content folders shown as header tabs | `navigation.tabs`                                                            |
| `seo` / `useSeoMeta` defaults                  | `seo.metatags`                                                               |
| `content.highlight` themes                     | drop and report                                                              |
| Search (Algolia DocSearch, built-in)           | drop and report                                                              |
| Analytics modules, custom plugins, middleware  | drop and report                                                              |
| i18n (`@nuxtjs/i18n`)                          | `navigation.languages` if the user migrates other languages, else report     |

## Navigation

Use the navigation tree from `_payload.json` (look for a `navigation` key at the top level or under `data`) or, in a repo, the ordered `content/` tree. Each node has `title`, `_path` or `path`, and `children`. Nodes with children become nested groups; their own page, if any, goes first in the group.

Labels: the node `title` is the sidebar label. If it differs from the page H1, set `sidebarTitle`. Drop numeric prefixes from paths and labels. Respect `navigation: false` in page front matter (page exists but is hidden) and `navigation.title` / `navigation.icon` overrides. Nuxt icons are usually Iconify names (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Icons).

## Content conversion

Walk the AST and emit markdown and Mintlify components. Count every distinct `tag` across the mirror first (`mint migrate --topic conversion`):

```python
import json, glob, collections
tags = collections.Counter()
def walk(n):
    if isinstance(n, dict):
        if 'tag' in n: tags[n['tag']] += 1
        for v in n.values(): walk(v)
    elif isinstance(n, list):
        if n and isinstance(n[0], str) and len(n) > 1 and isinstance(n[1], dict): tags[n[0]] += 1
        for v in n: walk(v)
for f in glob.glob('mirror/*.json'):
    walk(json.load(open(f)))
print(tags.most_common())
```

| MDC / component                                                               | Mintlify                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `::callout`, `::note`, `::tip`, `::warning`, `::caution`, `::alert{type=...}` | `<Note>`, `<Tip>`, `<Warning>`, `<Danger>`, `<Info>` by meaning |
| `::steps`, `::Steps` with `###` children                                      | `<Steps>` / `<Step title>`                                      |
| `::tabs` / `::code-group`                                                     | `<Tabs>` / `<CodeGroup>`                                        |
| `::card`, `::card-group`, `::card-grid`                                       | `<Card>`, `<CardGroup>`                                         |
| `::collapsible`, `::accordion`                                                | `<Accordion>`, `<AccordionGroup>`                               |
| `::field`, `::field-group`                                                    | `<ParamField>` / `<ResponseField>`                              |
| `::badge`, `:badge[...]`                                                      | `<Badge>`                                                       |
| `:icon{name=...}`                                                             | `<Icon icon="...">` (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Icons)  |
| `pre` with `filename`, `highlights` props                                     | fenced block with filename and `{1,3}` line highlights          |
| `prose-*` tags (`prose-h2`, `prose-a`, ...)                                   | the plain markdown element                                      |
| Site-specific components (custom `components/content/*.vue`)                  | (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Components)                 |

Hazards:

- Inline MDC attributes (`text{.class}`, `[link]{target=_blank}`) must be stripped; they are not MDX.
- Props in the AST (`:prop` bindings, `v-bind`) are data, not text. Do not dump them into the page.
- Front matter blocks inside components (`---` YAML inside `::card`) are props.
- Vue components with slots (`#title`, `#default`) map to component props and children.

## Assets

Images are under `public/` in the repo, or `/_nuxt/` and `/images/` on the live site (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Images and files). Nuxt Image (`<NuxtImg>`, `/_ipx/` URLs) serves resized variants: strip the `/_ipx/<modifiers>/` prefix to get the original file.

## URLs and redirects

Nuxt Content paths are the `content/` paths with numeric prefixes and `index` removed (`content/1.guide/0.index.md` → `/guide`). Keep those paths. Port redirects defined in `nuxt.config.ts` `routeRules` (`mint migrate --topic navigation`, Redirects).

## Known gaps

- Custom Vue components and interactive playgrounds: static content only.
- `app.config.ts` UI theming beyond primary color, logo and fonts.
- Built-in or Algolia search configuration, analytics modules.
- Content queries rendered on the page (`ContentList`, `ContentQuery`): migrate the rendered output as static content.
- Iconify icons with no Font Awesome equivalent.
